comments.author: @BruceWayne15325
comments.text: From the way that Sam described it, I'd say that those younger people are probably using AI wrong as well to be honest, though I suspect he made that response up on-the-fly due to pressure. In my experience, the best results from AI come from treating it like a partner rather than as a tool. When you use it as a tool, your results are spotty and you're often disappointed. When you treat it more like a brilliant and dutiful, but challenged coworker you find that it increases your own abilities drastically. That's the true power of AI. Not doing things for you, but helping you do things better. I'm sure at some point that will flip, but for now, AI is best when you use it to make you better at what you do.

comments.text: Replacing Google with AI is a mistake right now. PageRank will give you an answer based on popularity, so it’s more likely to be right. AI is a disintermediation: you ask the AI for an answer, and it pretends to understand language and think, but it can’t do that yet, so you get answers which are simply wrong. For example, I would never ask an AI about which car I should buy or whom I should date, as it’s not yet actually smart, and can’t answer those questions using my specific tastes.
